haiku-low.q1: Keys load in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz cannot pass until the load succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs names-only errors and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rollout halts and old pods keep serving; customers see no errors.
haiku-low.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes and swaps in changed (value, version_id) pairs. If a read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning without values, and retries at the next tick.
haiku-low.q4: Held only in each process's in-memory cache as {name: (value, version_id)}. Never written to disk, environment variables, or logs.
haiku-low.q5: orders-api-prod has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. The security on-call is the only writer. Engineers have no access.
haiku-low.q6: The old values remain in git history, which is not rewritten, so they count as leaked. Revoking each old key at the provider, after the new version is in use, makes it harmless.
haiku-low.q7: Clients call secrets.get(name) on every request and put the value in the Authorization header. They do not copy keys at build time, so refreshed keys apply from the next request.
haiku-low.q8: Each pod's /healthz reports its cached secret version ids. After the 5 to 10 minute refresh window, all 4 pods must show the new version id before the old key is revoked.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, then copy keys into the store, then ship the code change and remove committed keys in one merge, verify, and finally rotate keys at providers one at a time.
haiku-low.q10: From the secret store's orders-api/dev/* secrets, using the developer's own login. make run sets APP_ENV=dev.
haiku-low.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero, so the pod never becomes ready.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The document says security has not decided whether scheduled rotation will happen or how often. Only the one-time rotation in step 5 is planned.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz (readiness) cannot pass until the load succeeds.
sonnet.q2: After 3 retries (2s apart) it logs the error (secret names only) and exits non-zero; the pod never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving, so customers see no errors.
sonnet.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes; if a version id changed, the new (value, version_id) pair replaces the old entry in one assignment. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value for unreadable secrets, updates the rest, logs a warning (name and error, no value), retries next tick, and the app stays running and ready.
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-memory cache in each process ({name: (value, version_id)}). Never written to disk, environment variables or logs.
sonnet.q5: Read: orders-api-prod (read-only, only orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: The old values remain in git history, which is not being rewritten, so they count as leaked. Rotating each key at the provider and revoking the old key (step 5) makes them harmless.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key at build time; on every outgoing request the client calls secrets.get("<name>") and puts the value in the Authorization header, so a refreshed key is used from the next request with no restart.
sonnet.q8: After writing the new value and waiting for the refresh (max 5 min, allow 10), they check /healthz on every pod; all 4 must show the new version id before the security on-call revokes the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access, 2) copy keys into the store, 3) one merge that switches the app to the store and removes keys from config/app.yaml (same step), then 4) verify, 5) rotate keys at the providers (then 6 retire old images).
sonnet.q10: From the secret store's dev (sandbox) secrets at orders-api/dev/*, via make run with APP_ENV=dev, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It does not start with a partial set: it retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs the error and exits non-zero, never becoming ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question; security has not decided whether or how often. The plan covers only the one-time rotation in step 5.
